abstract.text:
Generalized uncertainty principle puts forward the existence of the shortest distances and/or maximum momentum at the Planck scale for consideration. In this article, we investigate the solutions
of a two-dimensional Duffin-Kemmer-Petiau (DKP) oscillator within an external magnetic field in
a minimal length (ML) scale. First, we obtain the eigensolutions in ordinary quantum mechanics.
Then, we examine the DKP oscillator in the presence of an ML for the spin-zero and spin-one
sectors. We determine an energy eigenvalue equation in both cases with the corresponding eigenfunctions in the non-relativistic limit. We show that in the ordinary quantum mechanic limit, where
the ML correction vanishes, the energy eigenvalue equations become identical with the habitual
quantum mechanical ones. Finally, we employ the Euler-Mclaurin summation formula and obtain
the thermodynamic functions of the DKP oscillator in the high-temperature scale.

citations.context:
During recent years, the number of extensive research subjected to the Generalized Uncertainty Principle (GUP)
in quantum mechanics [1], quantum electrodynamics [2], quantum cosmology [3], quantum gravity [4], black-hole
physics [5], and its thermodynamics [6] have increased.

In the past hundred years, exact or approximate solutions to the Schrödinger equation have been investigated to
describe the physical processes in the OQM [12–14].

This non-relativistic equation has also been examined within the
GUP perspective [15–19].

In particular, Bhat et al. calculated the correction term to the energy eigenvalue function
of a gravitational quantum well, by employing infinite extra dimensions [18].

The Klein-Gordon(KG) and the Dirac equations were frequently used in studies examining relativistic physical
processes [20–25].

For example, in the presence of the ML, Jana et al. obtained an exact solution to the KG equation by employing a linear and vector
potential energy [26].
In 2018, Boumali et al. investigated a two dimensional KG oscillator under the GUP [27].

In another study, Elviyanti et al. employed Asymptotic Iteration Method to examine the Hultén potential energy in the
KG equation in the ML [28].

Additionally, in 2013, Menculini et al. studied the relativistic Landau problem in Dirac
equation within the presence of the ML and reported an exact solution of the wave function in the momentum space
[29].

They concluded that the solution that was found by Menculini et al. was a subset of the general solution
which was correlated with the even quantum numbers [30].

Ikot et al. examined the two-dimensional harmonic
oscillator problem within the framework of ML on the Dirac equation in the commutative and noncommutative space,
respectively [31].

They announced that their results could predict the upper bound of the GUP parameter of the relativistic Landau
levels in graphene [32].
Duffin-Kemmer-Petiau (DKP) equation is another relativistic equation that appeared a century ago [33–36].

However, after then, it was comprehended that in special
cases that involve a symmetry breaking and hadronic processes, the solution of the DKP equation differs from those
of other equations [37].

For example, Boumali et al. investigated a two dimensional DKP oscillator under the effect
of a magnetic field [37].
Falek et al. investigated a three dimensional DKP oscillator [38].

Moreover, they considered
a deformed DKP oscillator with Snyder-de Sitter algebra in a momentum space with and without a magnetic field
[39, 40].

One of the authors of this article, Aounallah with his collaborator, obtained exact solutions of the DKP
equation with Aharonov-Bohm and Coulomb potential energies in the commutative [41] and non commutative [42]
space-times which are assumed to be produced by a cosmic string.

Hosseinpour et al. discussed the dynamic of the
DKP particles in the space-time that are initiated with a spinning cosmic string [43].

Wang et al. studied the spin-one
sector of the DKP oscillator in non commutative space in two dimension [44, 45].

Hun et al. considered the DKP
oscillator in a curved space-time [46].

In particular, Lunardi, he discussed the equivalency of the spin-one and spin-zero representation
of the DKP equation in one dimension [47].

Chargui revisited the DKP equation with linear potential energies in one
dimension and reported some inaccurate discussions in the literature [48].

We
observe that scientists have begun to discuss the thermal properties of the models they are handling [49–51].
One of the pioneering work in this area was given by Pacheco et al. in 2003 [52].
Later, they extended their work to three dimensions [53].
Nouicer analyzed a one-dimensional Dirac oscillator in the presence of the ML and examined its statistical properties [54].
Hamil et al. studied the Dirac and KG oscillators and reported their thermal properties on anti-de Sitter space [55].
Wu et al. investigated thermodynamic functions of a two-dimensional DKP oscillator in the GUP formalism [56].

The effects of the external magnetic field and the presence of the ML on the thermal quantities in a two-dimensional
Dirac oscillator are explored [57, 58].
This result is in agreement with [37].
This result corrects the typo of Eq. (48) in [37].

Instead, some authors employed
Eqs. (48), (49), (50) and (54) to build a correlation among the third, fourth, fifth and ninth components [37, 56].
Instead of following that ansatz, we examine the spin-one case in another formalism as given in [38–40].
To the best of our knowledge, there is no known exact solution to this equation [39].
We find the non relativistic energy eigenvalue function as follows [60]:

We employ the Heisenberg algebra representation on the momentum space where the momentum and position operators act on a momentum space wave
function as given [8]
Then, we follow the paper of Jana et al. [26].

Moreover, in another limit, where the external magnetic field does not exist, the cyclotron frequency vanishes and the energy eigenvalue function becomes
identical to the one given in Eq. (34) in [56].
Similarly to the spin-zero case, we follow the paper of Jana et al. [26].
This type of equation admits solutions in terms of hypergeometric functions [59].
Thus, we guarantee that the stability of the ensemble [53].
We employ the Euler-Mclaurin summation formula to compute the partition function as done in [39, 40, 54].

Therefore at higher temperatures, their contributions
become negligible and we ignore them [39, 40, 54].

Furthermore, in the absence of the external magnetic field in the OQM limit we obtain the well-known thermodynamic
functions of a scalar bosonic oscillator [39].

In the literature,
it is noted that the Euler-MacLaurin approximation is appropriate for high-temperatures [61] and the low-temperature
behaviors can be examined by adopting the method based on the Hurwitz zeta function [62].

abstract.text:
Generalized uncertainty principle puts forward the existence of the shortest distances and/or maximum momentum at the Planck scale for consideration. In this article, we investigate the solutions
of a two-dimensional Duffin-Kemmer-Petiau (DKP) oscillator within an external magnetic field in
a minimal length (ML) scale. First, we obtain the eigensolutions in ordinary quantum mechanics.
Then, we examine the DKP oscillator in the presence of an ML for the spin-zero and spin-one
sectors. We determine an energy eigenvalue equation in both cases with the corresponding eigenfunctions in the non-relativistic limit. We show that in the ordinary quantum mechanic limit, where
the ML correction vanishes, the energy eigenvalue equations become identical with the habitual
quantum mechanical ones. Finally, we employ the Euler-Mclaurin summation formula and obtain
the thermodynamic functions of the DKP oscillator in the high-temperature scale.

During recent years, the number of extensive research subjected to the Generalized Uncertainty Principle (GUP)
in quantum mechanics [1], quantum electrodynamics [2], quantum cosmology [3], quantum gravity [4], black-hole
physics [5], and its thermodynamics [6] have increased.

In the past hundred years, exact or approximate solutions to the Schrödinger equation have been investigated to
describe the physical processes in the OQM [12–14].

This non-relativistic equation has also been examined within the
GUP perspective [15–19].

In particular, Bhat et al. calculated the correction term to the energy eigenvalue function
of a gravitational quantum well, by employing infinite extra dimensions [18].

The Klein-Gordon(KG) and the Dirac equations were frequently used in studies examining relativistic physical
processes [20–25].

For example, in the presence of the ML, Jana et al. obtained an exact solution to the KG equation by employing a linear and vector
potential energy [26].
In 2018, Boumali et al. investigated a two dimensional KG oscillator under the GUP [27].
In another study, Elviyanti et al. employed Asymptotic Iteration Method to examine the Hultén potential energy in the KG equation in the ML [28].

Additionally, in 2013, Menculini et al. studied the relativistic Landau problem in Dirac
equation within the presence of the ML and reported an exact solution of the wave function in the momentum space
[29].

They concluded that the solution that was found by Menculini et al. was a subset of the general solution
which was correlated with the even quantum numbers [30].

oscillator problem within the framework of ML on the Dirac equation in the commutative and noncommutative space,
